transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I suppose I came in because of my in-laws. We've been arguing, but... I know it's not just a normal argument. They're... they've been using the altar. And the parish committee. Just trying to push me out... to make everyone forget what I've done for this family.
Do you really believe your in-laws are using the altar and parish committee against you?
Yes. I know they are. It's... it's not just a feeling. They're using the church... the altar... to turn everyone against me. To erase everything I've done.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people cannot hear?

I... well. I don't know if it's what you mean. But... yes. 

A few nights... I heard my mother. She's passed on, but... she was telling me where to put the marigolds and the candles. My husband said he didn't hear anything. And... one time, I saw her, too. Just standing by the kitchen doorway. He told me no one was there... but I know she was.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'erase everything I've done'?

Well... it's just what I said. They don't want anyone to remember. I raised the children... I kept the house together. But now... they want it all gone. So they use the altar. And the committee. Just... plotting to make sure I don't matter anymore. That's all.
Can you explain to me in a step-by-step way how you think the altar and parish committee are being used against you?

I don't... I can't really give you a list. It's just what I know. 

I came in here because... well, I knew my in-laws weren't just arguing with me anymore. It's more than that. They use the altar... and they talk to the parish committee... just to push me out. To make everyone forget everything I've done for this family. 

I don't really know how else to explain it. That's just what they're doing.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'they use the altar'?

I just... I already told you. They use it. My in-laws, they... they go there and they use it to turn the committee against me. I don't know how else to say it. They just want me gone, and they want everything I've done erased. That's it.
Can you tell me something that happened to you recently, and how it made you feel, in as much detail as you can?
I don't really know what you want me to say. I just... I sit at home mostly. I was making tea the other day, and... I just felt tired. That's all. There's not much to tell.
Can you describe your thought process when you're thinking about your in-laws using the altar against you?

Look, I don't really have a... a thought process about it. I don't sit around analyzing it. 

I'm just telling you why I'm here, like I already said. It stopped being just normal arguing with my in-laws a while ago. Now they're actually using the altar, and getting the parish committee involved, and... it's all just to push me out of the picture. They want to make sure everyone forgets everything I've done for this family. 

There isn't a process to describe. It's just what is happening. I don't know why you keep asking me to break it down.
Do you often find it difficult to express your thoughts in a logical and coherent way?
No... I don't think so. I mean, I'm talking to you right now, aren't I? I just... I don't always want to talk. That doesn't mean I can't.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are disjointed or hard to follow?

I don't... no. My thoughts are fine. I know what I'm thinking. It's just... sometimes it's hard to explain it to someone else, especially when they keep asking so many questions. But I can follow my own thoughts just fine.
Do you feel like your thoughts are racing or speeding by when you're thinking about your in-laws and the altar?
No, they don't race. I just... I think about what they're doing. That's all.
Do you feel like you jump from one idea to another when talking about your in-laws?
No... I don't do that. I just stick to what I'm saying about them. There's no jumping around.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disconnected from each other when you're thinking about your situation?
No... I don't. They aren't disconnected. Everything makes perfect sense to me. I don't really know why you keep asking about my thoughts. They're just normal.
When you're thinking about your in-laws using the altar against you, do you find it hard to stay on one topic?
No. I stay on it just fine. I... I know exactly what they're doing, so I focus on that. I don't lose track of it.
Do you feel like you have trouble getting your point across when talking about your in-laws and their alleged plot against you?
No... I don't have trouble with that. I tell it exactly how it is. If people don't want to listen to me, that's on them. I make my point just fine.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disorganized when you're thinking about your in-laws and the altar?
No... they're not disorganized. I know what they're doing. It's all very clear.
Do you often find yourself having trouble sticking to one topic when talking about things in general?
No... not really. I just talk about what I need to.
Has your situation with your in-laws and their alleged use of the altar against you caused you significant distress or problems in your daily life or relationships?

Well... yes, I suppose. I couldn't really... keep up with the parish preparations anymore. Or the house. My family had to step in and handle the festival tasks. My husband... he started staying close by. I guess I was missing meals and... not keeping up with my usual routines. I just wasn't taking care of things like I normally do.
Do you think your in-laws are actually capable of using the altar to erase your past contributions to the family?

Yes. I... I know they are. That's why I'm here. It's not just a normal argument, you know? They are... they're using the altar. And the parish committee. They're using it to push me out completely. To make everyone just... forget everything I've done for this family.
Do you feel like you have trouble organizing your thoughts when you're not talking about your in-laws?
No... I don't think so. I can think fine.
